open_errors.issue: Devan thinks he 'knew nothing of its stairs' and knew only that Neela would go 'where the city was loudest'. In ch 2 Neela told him Usha's exact line ('come by the sea stair at the noon gun'), and in ch 3 the plan was argued in front of him. He knows the sea stair and the hour.
open_errors.fix: Have Devan recall the sea-stair-at-the-noon-gun plan he was told on the hill.

patches.find: He knew nothing of its stairs. He knew only that, the night before she left, she had told him she would go where the city was loudest, because in a loud place no one hears a quiet thing. In Kodiyur the loud thing was the noon gun.
patches.replace: He knew nothing of its stairs but one. Usha had named it on the hill, and Neela had said it again over the ash: the sea stair, at the noon gun. In a loud hour no one hears a quiet thing.

open_errors.issue: Neela recalls Usha's advice about the throat paste 'at the shelter'. At the shelter Usha spoke to Neela only in public and for 'a breath or two' at dawn, when she gave the leaf line. Nobody crossed the slab after dark. The cuff and paste warning came from Muthu at the water jars (ch 9).
open_errors.fix: Attribute the warning to Muthu by the water jars.

patches.find: *Don't touch it,* Usha had said, at the shelter. *Not once. A hand at the throat is a tell.*
patches.replace: *Don't touch it,* Muthu had said, by the water jars. *Not once. A hand at the throat is a tell.*

open_errors.issue: 'He had not repeated Asha's last words' implies Vellan has already said them once. At the boulder (ch 5) he only said she said something and withheld the words until ch 27.
open_errors.fix: Say he had not spoken of the words again since the boulder.

patches.find: He had not repeated Asha's last words since the pass, and Devan had not asked.
patches.replace: He had not spoken of Asha's last words again since the boulder, and Devan had not asked.

open_errors.issue: The Company reached the gorge only three days before ch 8 (descent ch 4, boulder ch 5), and Neela leaves the next dawn. Neither 'every day for a week' (ch 8) nor 'spent a week making' the cut (ch 10) fits.
open_errors.fix: Replace the week with the actual span.

patches.find: Devan had ridden past it every day for a week and had not looked up.
patches.replace: Devan had ridden past it every day since the boulder and had not looked up.

patches.find: Far behind and above her, in the cut he had spent a week making into a bad day of stone, he was already fighting.
patches.replace: Far behind and above her, in the cut he had spent his days making into a bad day of stone, he was already fighting.

open_errors.issue: Thulasi (hoof on a foreleg, so she was in shape) and Vellan (whose bear cleared the lane) were both among the fifteen in the sally. Counting them as 'one more' and 'one more' makes the count of hands off the wall sixteen when it should be fifteen.
open_errors.fix: Fold Thulasi and Vellan into the fifteen and correct the count.

patches.find: Fifteen hollow and flat on their mats until dusk. One more with a leg, and one more to sit by it.
patches.replace: Fifteen hollow and flat on their mats until dusk, one of them with a cracked leg, and another who would not leave her side.

patches.find: "That's sixteen hands off tomorrow's wall," Kamalakshi said.
patches.replace: "That's fifteen hands off tomorrow's wall," Kamalakshi said.

open_errors.issue: Ch 28 says Neela returned the eleven Resin House pages 'at first light'. At first light she was turning back over Devan (ch 26) and then going up the cut to the dying Vellan (ch 27).
open_errors.fix: Move the reading to after Vellan was carried down.

patches.find: At first light she had put the eleven Resin House pages back into their owners' hands, one by one, in the open sun, as she had promised.
patches.replace: Once Vellan was carried down she had put the eleven Resin House pages back into their owners' hands, one by one, in the open sun, as she had promised, if late.

open_errors.issue: Neela tells the queen of Chathu's sheaf 'They're not burned. I told you why.' She has never explained anything about these pages to the queen. The queen gave them to her to keep (ch 16), and Neela does not learn they are plain ink until ch 29.
open_errors.fix: Have Neela say the queen left them in her keeping.

patches.find: "Mine," she said. "Chathu wrote these at your table. They're not burned. I told you why."
patches.replace: "Mine," she said. "Chathu wrote these at your table. You left them in my keeping."

open_errors.issue: Neela says she had smelled the salt-and-clove-bark resin 'once before', on the sleeper at Nellimala. She also smelled it on the dead Thurai scout at the shelf in ch 8, where she named it the same smell.

patches.find: She had smelled it once before, on a sleeper by a half-built tower, among sixty-three tents on a slope where her mother's house had been.
patches.replace: She had smelled it on a dead scout at the shelf, and before that on a sleeper by a half-built tower, among sixty-three tents on a slope where her mother's house had been.
